thread:
lucy-support: FYI customer (acme-inc) opened an escalation — streaming responses consistently drop the final chunk after ~20s when their client reconnects with a fresh auth cookie. They see a 200 but the last event is missing, client then reconnects and gets the remainder as a new stream (duplicate billing).

acme-dev: repro steps: open chat stream -> idle for ~90s -> resume prompt -> stream starts, emits tokens for ~18-22s then cuts. No error in body, connection stays ESTABLISHED for a bit then client reconnects. Using CF in front, ALB -> our nginx proxy -> origin.

sam-eng: Can you paste a minimal request and response headers (esp Keep-Alive, Connection, x-forwarded-proto, cookie)? Also which Cloudflare plan / WAF rules? Might be connection half-close or upstream h2 window.

acme-dev: headers excerpt:

```
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Connection: keep-alive
Accept: text/event-stream
Cookie: session=eyJ..(rotated on reconnect)
User-Agent: acme-sdk/1.2.3

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Connection: keep-alive
```

maya-sre: Quick note: ALB idle timeout default = 60s. Cloudflare's proxy expects longer keepalive. If client idle > ALB idle, ALB might half-close upstream while CF still has TCP open. That can produce truncated/partial last chunks. Do we have tcpdump from the origin side showing FIN/ACK around the cut?

acme-dev: attaching pcap snippet (excerpt):

```
... [origin -> ALB] FIN, ACK at 00:00:18.354 -> then client keepalive probes from Cloudflare at 00:00:19.100 -> new connection from client at 00:00:23.221
```

jordan-plat: Two possible contributing factors:
- nginx proxy/nginx buffering + sendfile behavior can buffer and only flush on connection close.
- If upstream (our app) is using HTTP/2 to ALB/Envoy, H2 stream reset semantics differ and intermediate proxies may drop trailing data when they see connection half-close.

sam-eng: Repro plan suggestion:
1) Set ALB idle timeout to 300s (match CF) for the target group.
2) Disable nginx proxy buffer for the SSE location: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;`
3) Have client use `Connection: close` on final chunk/explicit event to force flush, or send a sentinel event before quiet periods.

lucy-support: Customer asked for quick mitigation they can apply on their side — they control the CF zone. They can enable "origin keepalive" and set proxy_read_timeout higher. They also asked if there's anything we can change server-side.

maya-sre: On our side we should ensure backend runtime calls flush after each token (we already call fflush on the response writer, but nginx buffering can still hold). Priorities:
- Short term: update ALB target group's idle timeout to 300s for affected customer (needs infra change and validated by infra team).
- Short term: add an explicit SSE heartbeat event every 15s from origin to keep connection active.
- Medium: add a detection path in the proxy that logs a mismatch between downstream TCP close and upstream app still writing (we can gate on `proxy_send_timeout` expirations).

acme-dev: They tried adding a 10s heartbeat and saw fewer truncations but still occasional missing final token on long idle -> suspect cookie/session swap race: when client reconnects with rotated cookie, CF opens a new connection to ALB while ALB still closing previous backend socket. That race can drop last chunk.

sam-eng: We should reproduce with a small harness: CF simulator -> ALB -> nginx -> simple SSE app that writes tokens every 250ms for 20s then idles 95s then writes final token. Automate cookie rotation at reconnect to mimic their auth proxy.

jordan-plat: For immediate support: recommend customer enable the CF "Disable HTTP/2 to origin" option for a test (forces h1 keepalive behavior) and set ALB idle timeout > 240s. Also turn on CF origin keepalive and increase `origin_read_timeout`.

lucy-support: I'll propose a short runbook for the customer and offer a dedicated infra change for ALB timeout if they want us to coordinate (escalation). Also logging request ids and adding `x-stream-offset` header will help detect dup billing.

deploy-bot: NOTE: infra ticket created INFRA-1229 to evaluate ALB idle-timeout baseline and opt-in for customer-targeted timeout changes.

acme-dev: Thanks everyone. We'll try the CF h1 test + heartbeat and report back. Appreciate the ALB ticket.

sam-eng: Followups:
- @maya-sre can you scope how much risk there is in raising ALB idle globally vs per-targetgroup?
- @jordan-plat can you help craft the SSE proxy config snippet we can provide to customers (nginx + envoy examples)?

maya-sre: Will check. Raising per-targetgroup is low-risk but global changes require load testing.

jordan-plat: I'll paste example configs shortly.

lucy-support: Marking this thread for escalation tracking. If the customer confirms reduced truncation after CF->ALB adjustments, we'll close. If not, we'll collect full packet captures and do deeper Envoy/nginx traces. :thumbsup:
